cguCitoyen.title: Terms of use — individuals
cguCitoyen.intro: These terms apply to anyone who uses AccesDirectAide for themselves, with or without an account.
cguCitoyen.operator.title: 1. Who provides the service
cguCitoyen.operator.p1: The service is provided by {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date.
cguCitoyen.free.title: 2. A free service
cguCitoyen.free.p1: The service is free. No payment is asked of you, either by AccesDirectAide or, through it, by a structure. The site contains no advertising.
cguCitoyen.noDecision.title: 3. What the service does not do
cguCitoyen.noDecision.p1: AccesDirectAide is not a government website. It helps you find information, check whether an aid may concern you and contact a structure. It takes no decision on your rights: only the competent body (Caf, CPAM, France Travail, Collectivité européenne d'Alsace, CCAS…) decides.
cguCitoyen.noDecision.p2: The information is given for guidance, with its official source and its date. It may change: check it with the source shown.
cguCitoyen.ai.title: 4. The automatic assistant
cguCitoyen.ai.p1: The assistant can search, explain and suggest a draft. It can make mistakes. It does not give legal advice and decides nothing.
cguCitoyen.ai.p2: Do not write in it any information about your health, a disability, your administrative situation or that of another person.
cguCitoyen.account.title: 5. Your account
cguCitoyen.account.i1: An account is needed to request an appointment.
cguCitoyen.account.i2: You must be 18 or over to create an account.
cguCitoyen.account.i3: You give accurate information and keep your password secret.
cguCitoyen.account.i4: Your account is personal: do not act on behalf of another person without their agreement.
cguCitoyen.appointments.title: 6. Appointments
cguCitoyen.appointments.p1: An appointment request is not a confirmed appointment. The structure confirms, offers another slot or declines. It may also change or cancel an appointment; you are informed in your space.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p2: You can cancel your request or your appointment from your space. Let them know as early as possible.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p3: Each structure sets its own reception rules. AccesDirectAide guarantees neither an available place nor the granting of an aid.
cguCitoyen.appointments.p4: The message attached to a request is optional. It is passed on only with your agreement, which you can withdraw at any time from your space.
cguCitoyen.use.title: 7. Proper use
cguCitoyen.use.i1: Do not publish or send content that is unlawful, abusive or harmful to another person.
cguCitoyen.use.i2: Do not try to access other people's data or to disrupt the service.
cguCitoyen.use.i3: Do not use a program to extract content in bulk or to book slots.
cguCitoyen.deletion.title: 8. Deleting your account
cguCitoyen.deletion.p1: You can ask for your account to be deleted at any time, from your space or by writing to {{contact}}. A person checks the request before deletion, to avoid a mistake or identity theft.
cguCitoyen.deletion.p2: Some data may be kept for a limited period when an obligation or the defence of a right requires it; the privacy notice lists them.
cguCitoyen.deletion.p3: If the account is used in breach of these terms, it may be suspended. You are informed of the reason, except in a security emergency, and you can submit your comments.
cguCitoyen.liability.title: 9. Liability
cguCitoyen.liability.p1: The operator takes reasonable steps to keep the information accurate and the service available. They cannot guarantee that there is no error at all or that the service runs without interruption. Reported errors are corrected as soon as possible.
cguCitoyen.liability.p2: The operator is not responsible for the decisions of public bodies and structures, nor for the content of the external sites they link to.
cguCitoyen.liability.p3: The operator remains liable for their own faults under the conditions laid down by law. No clause of these terms reduces the rights the law gives you.
cguCitoyen.changes.title: 10. Changes and end of the service
cguCitoyen.changes.p1: These terms may change. Each version is published with its date. Before a significant change, account holders are informed and can delete their account.
cguCitoyen.changes.p2: If the service stops or is taken over by someone else, for example an association created later, account holders are informed in advance. No data is passed on without prior information.
cguCitoyen.law.title: 11. Applicable law and disputes
cguCitoyen.law.p1: These terms are governed by French law. If there is a problem, first write to {{contact}}: an amicable solution is sought.
cguCitoyen.law.p2: Consumer mediation: whether it applies to a free service published by a private individual, outside any professional activity, remains to be checked. No mediator has been appointed to date.
cguCitoyen.law.p3: Failing an amicable solution, you may bring the matter before the competent court under the ordinary rules.
cguCitoyen.law.p4: Only the French version of these terms is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
cguPro.title: Terms of use — professionals
cguPro.intro: These terms apply to professionals who use an ADA Pro account created at the invitation of their structure.
cguPro.operator.title: 1. Who provides the service
cguPro.operator.p1: The service is provided by {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. Contact: {{contact}}.
cguPro.operator.p2: The service is free for professionals and for their structure. Nothing is invoiced.
cguPro.account.title: 2. Your professional account
cguPro.account.i1: The account is created at the invitation of your structure. It is personal: do not share it.
cguPro.account.i2: Two-factor authentication is mandatory. Keep your sign-in means secret.
cguPro.account.i3: Your structure manages its team's access and deactivates your account when you leave it.
cguPro.use.title: 3. Use in the service of people
cguPro.use.i1: Use the account only for the tasks of your structure.
cguPro.use.i2: Open a person's information only when it is necessary for their request.
cguPro.use.i3: Do not copy this information outside the tools provided by your structure.
cguPro.use.i4: Respect professional secrecy and the rules of your structure.
cguPro.use.i5: Do not write health or disability data in a free-text field unless it is essential to the request.
cguPro.appointments.title: 4. Appointments
cguPro.appointments.p1: You confirm, offer another slot or decline the requests addressed to you, within a reasonable time. Keep your slots up to date.
cguPro.appointments.p2: Neither the platform nor its assistant decides any right. A draft suggested by the assistant must be checked before any use.
cguPro.data.title: 5. Your own data
cguPro.data.p1: For your account, the platform processes your name, your professional e-mail address, your role, your slots and the log of your actions. The privacy notice describes this processing, its proposed legal bases and its retention periods.
cguPro.data.p2: Your actions are logged for security and access control.
cguPro.incident.title: 6. Security incident
cguPro.incident.p1: Report without delay to {{contact}} any loss of a sign-in means, any suspicious access or any sending error.
cguPro.end.title: 7. Suspension and end
cguPro.end.p1: If the account is used in breach of these terms, it may be suspended. You and your structure are informed, except in a security emergency.
cguPro.liability.title: 8. Liability and applicable law
cguPro.liability.p1: Each party is liable for its own faults under the conditions laid down by law. The operator is not responsible for the decisions of your structure or of public bodies.
cguPro.liability.p2: These terms are governed by French law. If there is a problem, first write to {{contact}}.
cguPro.liability.p3: Only the French version of these terms is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
structures.title: Conditions for structures
structures.intro: These conditions describe the rules proposed to structures (associations, public services, establishments) that appear in the directory or receive appointment requests. No structure has signed them to date.
structures.directory.title: 1. Directory listing
structures.directory.p1: Listings come from official or public sources: FINESS, data·inclusion, the Annuaire de l'administration (Service-Public / DILA). Each listing shows its source and its date.
structures.directory.p2: A listing indicates that a service exists. It guarantees neither a place nor an admission.
structures.directory.p3: The structure can ask for its listing to be corrected or updated at {{contact}}.
structures.agreement.title: 2. Connection to appointments
structures.agreement.p1: To receive appointment requests, a written agreement is signed between the structure and the operator. It names a contact person. The connection is free: no sum is paid by the structure or to the structure.
structures.agreement.p2: The operator is {{operator}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. Contact: {{contact}}.
structures.roles.title: 3. Roles for personal data
structures.roles.p1: For what it receives (requests, contact details, message accepted by the person), the structure is the controller of its own processing, in its own files and according to its own obligations.
structures.roles.p2: For the handling of the request in the platform, the operator and the structure would be joint controllers (GDPR, art. 26). An arrangement will set this out; its essence will be made available to the people concerned.
structures.roles.p3: If the structure uses the tool as its own diary, the operator would act as a processor (GDPR, art. 28), under a written contract.
structures.commitments.title: 4. Commitments of the structure
structures.commitments.i1: Answer requests within a reasonable time and keep its slots up to date.
structures.commitments.i2: Manage its team's accounts: invite, remove rights and deactivate an account when a person leaves.
structures.commitments.i3: Inform people as its own obligations require.
structures.commitments.i4: Declare, before opening, the services whose nature may reveal health or disability data.
structures.commitments.i5: Apply a person's withdrawal of their agreement to the message: delete any copy, or keep it under its own responsibility and inform the person.
structures.sensitive.title: 5. Sensitive services
structures.sensitive.p1: Booking services whose nature may reveal health or disability data is closed to date. Opening it requires a « service sensible » indicator, the person's explicit consent and a check of the requirements for hosting health data (to be checked).
structures.operatorCommitments.title: 6. Commitments of the operator
structures.operatorCommitments.i1: Provide the service free of charge, with appropriate security measures.
structures.operatorCommitments.i2: Inform the structure without undue delay of any incident affecting the data that concern it.
structures.operatorCommitments.i3: Not use these data for other purposes and never sell them.
structures.end.title: 7. Duration, end and applicable law
structures.end.p1: Either party may end the connection with the notice period set in the agreement. At the end, the data are returned or deleted as the agreement provides.
structures.end.p2: Each party is liable for its own faults. These conditions are governed by French law; an amicable solution is sought first.
structures.end.p3: Only the French version of these conditions is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
privacyNotice.title: Privacy notice (GDPR, articles 13 and 14)
privacyNotice.intro: This notice explains which personal data AccesDirectAide processes, why, on what basis, for how long, and what your rights are.
privacyNotice.controller.title: 1. Controller
privacyNotice.controller.p1: The controller is {{controller}}, a natural person, who operates AccesDirectAide in a personal, voluntary capacity. No association has been created to date. No data protection officer has been appointed.
privacyNotice.controller.p2: For your data: {{contact}} or the contact form.
privacyNotice.status.title: 2. Status of this notice
privacyNotice.status.p1: This notice describes the processing for personal accounts (section 3). Appointments, messages, reminders and the sharing of files are not open yet: their legal bases are given as proposals (section 3a) and will be confirmed before they open.
privacyNotice.purposes.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases for personal accounts
privacyNotice.purposes.i1: P1 — Operation and security of the public site (technical logs, request rate limiting, security cookie « __csrf »): legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i2: P2 — Creating and keeping the account (verified e-mail address, protected password, « 18 or over » statement, proof of acceptance of the terms of use and of their version): performance of the contract formed by the terms of use (art. 6(1)(b)), for the data needed for the account only. Accepting the terms and the adult statement are not consents within the meaning of the GDPR. No telephone number is asked.
privacyNotice.purposes.i3: P2b — Optional display settings (text size, contrast, reduced animations, read aloud, easy-to-read French (FALC)): they are saved only in your browser, on your device (local storage). They are not sent to AccesDirectAide and are not saved in your account: we do not receive them. They therefore do not sync between your devices; on another device or browser you need to choose them again. They stay on the device after you sign out. You can change or reset them at any time (« Reset the display »), or erase them with your browser data. They are used only for the display you chose: they say nothing about your health or a disability, and no such information is asked. This storage on your device, made at your request to adapt the display, is not subject to a consent request (article 82 of the French Data Protection Act, « loi Informatique et Libertés »).
privacyNotice.purposes.i4: P3 — Sign-in and locking after several failed attempts: performance of the contract (art. 6(1)(b)) for signing in; legitimate interest in protecting accounts (art. 6(1)(f)) for the security measures.
privacyNotice.purposes.i5: P10a — Service e-mails about the account (address verification, password, change of address, account notices): performance of the contract (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i6: P12 — Log of administration actions: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes.i7: P13 — Exercise of your rights: legal obligation (art. 6(1)(c); articles 12 to 22 of the GDPR). Blocked retention (« hold ») of a specific piece of data: legal obligation when an authority or a court requires it (art. 6(1)(c)); otherwise, to establish, exercise or defend a legal claim, legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)) and, for sensitive data, art. 9(2)(f) — restricted access, duration limited to the dispute.
privacyNotice.purposes.i9: P15 — Erasure when the periods end: legal obligation (art. 6(1)(c); art. 5(1)(e) and 17 of the GDPR). Proof archives with restricted access (for example the proof of a consent or of a rights request): legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)), for the period given in section 4.
privacyNotice.purposes.i10: P16 — Technical providers: no basis of their own; they act on instructions (art. 28).
privacyNotice.purposes.p1: No purpose is based on a task carried out in the public interest. No decision producing legal effects is taken by automated means: the service decides no right.
privacyNotice.purposes.p2: Without an e-mail address no account can be created; optional fields can be left empty.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.title: 3a. Functions not open yet (proposed bases)
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i1: P4 — Searching for an appointment and showing the names of professionals: for you, performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); for professionals, legitimate interest of the operator and of their structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i2: P4p — Professionals' accounts, including their two-step verification: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)); performance of the professional terms they accept (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i3: P5 — Requesting, rescheduling, cancelling, confirming or declining an appointment, and the related service messages: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i4: P5s — Appointment with a service whose nature may reveal health or disability data: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)) and explicit consent (art. 9(2)(a)) through a separate box. This booking is not open.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i5: P6 — Optional message attached to a request: consent (art. 6(1)(a)) and explicit consent (art. 9(2)(a)), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i6: P7 — Assigning a professional to an appointment: performance of the terms (art. 6(1)(b)); « no preference » choice: legitimate interest of the structure (art. 6(1)(f)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i7: P8 — Referrals between professionals (closed feature): consent to each sharing (art. 6(1)(a); art. 9(2)(a)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i8: P9 — Shared files and follow-up (closed feature): consent to sharing (art. 6(1)(a); art. 9(2)(a)).
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i9: P10b/P10c — Reminder the day before and browser notifications: consent (art. 6(1)(a)), which can be withdrawn at any time.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.i10: P11 — Outlook availability of a structure (disabled): basis chosen by the structure; the operator acts on its behalf.
privacyNotice.purposes-later.p1: These processing operations are not in service. Their legal bases will be confirmed by the controller before they open; this notice will then be updated.
privacyNotice.retention.title: 4. Retention periods
privacyNotice.retention.i1: Account (e-mail address, protected password, display name, language, notification preferences): as long as you use it. You can ask for its erasure at any time from your account: a person checks the request, to prevent a mistake or identity theft, then erases the account within one month at most.
privacyNotice.retention.i2: Inactive account: an account without any activity on your part (sign-in) for 24 months may be erased. This erasure is not in service yet; before it is, this notice will say how you will be warned. Account never activated (e-mail address never confirmed): erased 7 days after its creation, together with the record of its sign-up.
privacyNotice.retention.i3: Address-verification, password and address-change links: valid for 15 minutes (30 minutes for an address change), then deleted.
privacyNotice.retention.i4: Sign-in session: 7 days at most. After 5 failed sign-ins, the account is locked for 15 minutes.
privacyNotice.retention.i5: Rate-limiting counters (your IP address and, for sign-in, account creation and the sending of links, a fingerprint of your e-mail address, never the address itself): erased at the end of their window, from a few minutes to one hour. The logs keep only a condensed fingerprint of them.
privacyNotice.retention.i6: Service e-mails: AccesDirectAide does not keep their content; the record of the sending (the message number at the provider) is kept 12 months. If an address permanently refuses messages, a fingerprint of the address (not the address itself) blocks sending; this block is reviewed after 12 months and removed if it is no longer justified.
privacyNotice.retention.i7: Restricted-access archives after an account is erased: proof of acceptance of the terms of use and of the « 18 or over » statement, 12 months; requests to exercise rights, 3 years after they are closed. They serve only to prove or defend in a dispute.
privacyNotice.retention.i8: Administration and security logs (without your e-mail address): 12 months.
privacyNotice.retention.i9: Blocked retention (« hold ») of a specific item, when an authority requires it or a dispute calls for it: until the end of the procedure; the record of its release is kept 12 months.
privacyNotice.retention.i10: Providers' technical logs: the host (Vercel) keeps its runtime logs from 1 hour to 1 day depending on the plan; the retention of the e-mail provider's logs (Mailjet) is being verified.
privacyNotice.retention.i11: Restoration history: encrypted backup copies, 35 days at most; database history at Neon, 6 hours at most. An erased item may remain in these copies for these periods; it is used only to repair an incident. So that a restoration cannot bring back an erased person, a record of each erasure (technical identifier of the account and of the request, date; no address or name) is kept for 40 days outside the database, at Upstash (Frankfurt).
privacyNotice.retention.i12: Functions not open yet (appointments, optional message, professionals' notifications, assistant): their periods will be announced in this notice before they open. For confirmed, attended or missed appointments, the intended period is 1 year after the appointment date, then anonymisation.
privacyNotice.retention.p1: None of these periods is imposed by a legal text: they are set by the controller. Automatic deletion at these deadlines is not yet fully switched on; you can ask for erasure at any time.
privacyNotice.recipients.title: 5. Recipients
privacyNotice.recipients.p1: Your data are neither sold nor rented. They are accessible to: the operator; the structure you choose for an appointment, for what is passed on to it; the technical providers below, on instructions.
privacyNotice.processors.title: 6. Technical providers (processors)
privacyNotice.processors.i1: Vercel Inc.: hosting of the site and of the server functions, run in Frankfurt.
privacyNotice.processors.i2: Neon (contract with Databricks, Inc.): database hosted in Frankfurt.
privacyNotice.processors.i3: Upstash, Inc.: security counters and request rate limiting, in Frankfurt.
privacyNotice.processors.i4: Mailjet (Sinch group): sending of service e-mails (address verification, password, account notices); data hosted by Google Cloud in Frankfurt (Germany) and Saint-Ghislain (Belgium).
privacyNotice.processors.i5: Microsoft: inbox of the contact address.
privacyNotice.processors.i6: Scaleway SAS (France) and Cloudflare, Inc.: backup copies of the database. The backup task runs at Scaleway, in Paris, and encrypts the copy before it is sent anywhere; Cloudflare stores it in the European Union without being able to read it.
privacyNotice.processors.p1: Each of these providers acts on instruction, under a data processing agreement (GDPR Article 28) incorporated into its terms of service.
privacyNotice.transfers.title: 7. Transfers outside the European Union
privacyNotice.transfers.p1: These providers belong to groups established in the United States: access from the United States is possible. The safeguards provided are the European Commission's standard contractual clauses (decision 2021/914) and, for Vercel, Upstash and Mailjet (Sinch), the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, according to their own terms. Scaleway SAS is the exception: it is a French company, which runs the backup task in Paris.
privacyNotice.rights.title: 8. Your rights
privacyNotice.rights.i1: Access, rectification, erasure and restriction of your data.
privacyNotice.rights.i2: Portability, for data processed on the basis of the terms of use or of your consent.
privacyNotice.rights.i3: Objection, for processing based on legitimate interest.
privacyNotice.rights.i4: Withdrawal of your consent at any time, as easily as you gave it. Withdrawal does not affect what was done before.
privacyNotice.rights.p1: Write to {{contact}}. You receive an answer within one month.
privacyNotice.rights.p2: You can also lodge a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr).
privacyNotice.booking.title: 9. When you request an appointment
privacyNotice.booking.p1: The chosen structure receives your name, your e-mail address, your telephone if you give it, the requested slot and, if you accepted, your message.
privacyNotice.booking.p2: For what it receives, the structure is the controller of its own processing: it decides what it does with it in its files, according to its own obligations. You can exercise your rights with it.
privacyNotice.booking.p3: For the handling of the request in the platform, the operator and the structure would be joint controllers; an arrangement will set this out and its essence will be published. No structure has signed an arrangement to date.
privacyNotice.sensitive.title: 10. Sensitive services (draft)
privacyNotice.sensitive.p1: Some services may reveal information about your health or a disability, for example a mental health or addiction service. An appointment request with these services would be processed only with your explicit consent, given through a separate unticked box. Withdrawing this consent would cancel the request.
privacyNotice.sensitive.p2: Booking these services is closed to date.
privacyNotice.art14.title: 11. Professionals and structure contacts (article 14)
privacyNotice.art14.p1: The directory contains information about structures and, where applicable, their professional contacts (name of the structure, address of the establishment, professional telephone and e-mail address, sometimes the name of a manager). It is not collected from you: it comes from official or public sources — FINESS, data·inclusion, the Annuaire de l'administration (Service-Public / DILA). Each listing shows its source and its date.
privacyNotice.art14.p2: Purpose: informing the public about the services that exist. Proposed basis: legitimate interest (art. 6(1)(f)). Proposed period: as long as the source publishes the information; updated at each import.
privacyNotice.art14.p3: If your structure creates a professional account for you, it provides your name and professional address: sections 3 to 8 also apply to you.
privacyNotice.art14.p4: You can ask for a correction or object to the display of data about you: {{contact}}.
privacyNotice.language.title: 12. Reference language
privacyNotice.language.p1: Only the French version of this notice is legally authoritative; translations are an aid to understanding.
